summary: Verified the Bearer-token fallback fix for the reported 'unable to sign in' bug and the Emergent Object Storage cheque flow. Backend: 24/25 pytest cases pass in /app/backend/tests/test_auth_bearer_and_cheque.py — login returns access_token in body AND HttpOnly cookie, wrong password returns 401 with no token, Bearer-only auth works on /auth/me, /dashboard, /snapshots, /officers, /reasons, cookie-only regression still works, follow-ups create successfully for all 3 outcomes with either auth style, assignment endpoint works, all 6 sort options return 114 parties with correct ordering (name_desc now truly reverse alphabetical, code_desc sinks empty codes to bottom), cheque upload → returns {url,filename,storage_path} with url=/api/uploads/cheques/<file>, DB cheque_files record created, GET /api/uploads/cheques/<file> serves image bytes via BOTH Bearer and cookie auth, non-image rejected with 400. Frontend UI (Playwright on preview URL): 8/8 checks pass — wrong password shows login-error 'Incorrect email or password' and does NOT store a token; correct login stores sripati_access_token in localStorage and reaches dashboard; hard reload keeps user signed in (interceptor attaches Bearer on the initial /auth/me); logout clears localStorage token AND cookie, /auth/me returns 401 afterward, login form is shown again. Only failing pytest case is a test-side name-string mismatch for 'C.B. CREATION' when re-fetched via GET /snapshots/{id}/parties (party name in DB likely has slightly different punctuation) — J TEX INDIA ₹1,91,702, 114 parties, ₹2.33 Cr grand total all verified. No user-visible bug remains.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 773 lines with auth, parser, storage helpers, and all routes in one file — the earlier suggestion to split into auth.py / parser.py / storage.py / routes/*.py still stands.

get_object() forwards the upstream Content-Type response header but serve_cheque prefers the DB-stored content_type; harmless but the get_object() second return value is effectively unused — consider dropping it for simplicity.

put_object()/get_object() retry once on 404 by re-initing storage key; still no retry on 401/403 which can happen if the storage session key is revoked out-of-band. Consider making the retry also cover those two.

Response interceptor in api.js clears the stored token on ANY 401 except /auth/login. That's correct but also means a single stale-token 401 on a background endpoint will silently sign the user out on next request. Consider a small delay/backoff or a one-time refresh attempt before nuking the token.
make_token() uses HS256 with JWT_SECRET from env — good. But there is no token refresh endpoint; users are forcibly logged out after 8h even mid-session. Consider adding /api/auth/refresh.

rca of the issue: Original 'unable to sign in' bug: real-user browsers were silently dropping the HttpOnly SameSite=None cookie (Safari ITP, Chrome partitioned/third-party cookie restrictions, corporate proxies). Fix layered a Bearer-token fallback: (a) /api/auth/login now returns access_token in JSON body, (b) frontend axios client persists it in localStorage under 'sripati_access_token' and attaches Authorization: Bearer via request interceptor, (c) response interceptor clears the token on 401 except during /auth/login, (d) login form clears any stale token before submitting, (e) logout clears both cookie and localStorage. Backend current_user() already accepted cookie OR header so nothing else changed. Verified: with cookies stripped, all protected endpoints work with just the Bearer header; with the Authorization header stripped, cookie flow still works (regression guard); hard reload keeps user signed in on real preview URL.
